1  THIS MFA IS FILED U/S.173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 15.04.2021 PASSED IN MVC NO.1732/2018 ON THE FILE OF THE PRL.
SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MEMBER, MACT, SRIRANGAPATANA, DISMISSING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING THIS DAY,
K.S.MUDAGAL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT
Aggrieved by the dismissal of his petition the claimant in MVC No.1732/2018 on the file of Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Srirangapatna has preferred this appeal.

2. On 31.10.2018 at 8.30 p.m. when the appellant was riding motorcycle bearing registration No.KA.02-JR-4103 near Shiva Gowri Kalyana Mantapa, Chamanahalli village within the limits of Bannur police station, T. Narasipura Taluk, he met with an accident.

entities.text: Bannur police station, T. Narasipura Taluk
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: One Shivaraju allegedly filed complaint on 01.11.2018 at 7.15 p.m. before the Bannur police as per Ex.P2.
Contending that the Canter vehicle bearing registration No.KA.10-1194 came in a high-speed, rash and negligent manner hit the appellant, causing the accident.
It was further alleged that the appellant suffered grievous injuries.
On the basis of such complaint, Bannur police registered the FIR as per Ex.P1 in Crime No.365/2018 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 IPC and under Section 187 of IMV Act, 1988.
On investigation, the said police filed charge sheet as per Ex.P7 against the driver of the Canter vehicle bearing registration No.KA.10-1194.

At the relevant time, respondent Nos.1 and 2 were the registered owner and insurer of the Canter vehicle bearing registration No.KA.10-1194.
3.

The claimant filed MVC No.1732/2018 claiming compensation of Rs.42,00,000/- from the respondents on the ground that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Canter vehicle bearing registration No.KA.10-1194.
It was further alleged that due to the injuries suffered in the accident the appellant has suffered permanent physical disability.

4. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 contested the petition denying the negligence on the part of the driver of Canter vehicle, age, occupation, income of the appellant and their liability to pay the compensation.
5. In support of his case, the appellant got himself examined as PW.1.
The doctor of Nagarajegowda Memorial Hospital, Mysuru was examined as CW.1.
On his behalf Exs.P.1 to 13 and Ex.C1 to C11 were marked.
Respondent No.1 did not adduce any evidence.

On behalf of respondent No.2 the insurer, the medical officer of Bannur Community Medical Center was examined as RW.1 and the official of company was examined as RW.2 and Ex.R.1 the MLC register extract of Bannur community medical center was marked.
6. The Tribunal on hearing the parties by the impugned order dismissed the petition on the ground that the claimant has failed to prove that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Sri. Mahadeva vs Sri. Huchegowda on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137471706/
2 Canter vehicle bearing registration No.KA.10-1194.

The Tribunal held that the complainant himself took the appellant to Bannur Community Medical Center with a history of self-fall, there was delay in filing the complaint and alleged eye witness Shivaraju was not examined.

Submission of Sri Vijay Kumar T, learned Counsel for the appellant:
7.
On thorough investigation, the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the Canter vehicle and that was not challenged by the respondent.
The insurer in para No.5 of the written statement admitted the involvement of the Canter lorry in the accident.
Under such circumstance, the Tribunal was in error in disbelieving those documents.
The appellant was taken to Mysuru hospital with a history of accident involving the Canter vehicle.
The Tribunal committed error in rejecting Ex.C11 and the evidence of CW.1.

Submissions of Smt. Manjula Tejaswini, learned Counsel for respondent No.2:
8.
Admittedly the appellant was first taken to Bannur hospital and the complainant Shivaraju himself gave history of self-fall.
Under such circumstances to rebut the said document, the appellant should have examined the said Shivaraju.
Adverse inference has to be drawn against him for not examining Shivaraju.
The evidence of CW.1 and Ex.C11 show that CW.1 is not the author of the entries in Ex.C11 relating to the appellant.
Therefore the same was not proved.
The statement in para No.5 of the written statement of respondent No.2 cannot be called as an admission as the same is not unequivocal and unambiguous.
In the immediate successive paragraph of the written statement, respondent No.2 has disputed the involvement of the insured vehicle and negligence on the part of the driver of the said vehicle.
Therefore the statement in para No.5 of the written statement cannot be called as an admission.
The IMV report Ex.P5 goes contrary to the case of the appellant.
The charge sheet is not a conclusive proof.
It was for the claimant to prove the occurrence of the accident and the involvement of the vehicle.

9. In support of her submission, she relies on the following judgments;
(i) Veerappa and another Vs Siddappa and  Another1  (ii) North West Karnataka Road Transport  Corporation Vs Gourabai and others 10.

entities.text: Veerappa and another Vs Siddappa and  Another1  (ii)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: North West Karnataka Road Transport  Corporation Vs Gourabai and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having regard to the submissions of both side and examining the records, the point that arises for consideration is "whether the finding of the Tribunal that the appellant/claimant failed to prove that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Canter vehicle bearing registration No.KA.10-1194 suffers illegality and is improper?
Analysis Sri. Mahadeva vs Sri. Huchegowda on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137471706/

3 11. The first and foremost contention of the appellant is that since the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the Canter vehicle bearing registration No.KA.10-1194, the Tribunal ILR 2009 KAR 3562 (2009) 12 SCC 165 should not have traversed beyond that.

Therefore the question is "whether the charge sheet is the conclusive proof barring the Tribunal from appreciating the other evidence on record?".
12.

The Coordinate bench of this Court in Veerappa's case referred to supra taking judicial notice of ambulance chasers operating syndicate of Police, Medical Officer, Motor Vehicle Inspector etc., to make wrongful gain planting a vehicle which has insurance, in para No.16 of the judgment held as follows:
"16. Sub-Section (2) of Section 149 provides the grounds on which the insurance company can avoid the liability to pay the compensation under the Act.
One such ground is, if a policy is obtained by a representation of fact which was false in some material particular.

Section 172 confers on the Claims Tribunal a power to award compensatory costs, if it is satisfied that the policy of insurance is void on the ground that it was obtained by representation of fact which was false in any material particular or any party or insured has put forward a false or vexatious claim or defence.
Sub-Section (3) of Section 172 also speaks of criminal liability in respect of such misrepresentation.
However, it restricts the compensatory costs to be awarded to only Rs.1,000/-.
Therefore, the Act provides for taking action against a party who sets up a false or vexatious defence.
However, the cost of Rs.1,000/- prescribed under the aforesaid provision, has failed to act as a sufficient deterrent to the parties setting up false claim or defence.
The experience has shown that this branch of law is slowly getting into the hands of unscrupulous people who are making a mockery of judicial process.
A disturbing trend of unholy alliance among the police, the doctors, the lawyers and sometimes even the Insurance Company, to siphon out the public money, and make an unlawful gain is fast emerging.
It is also gaining respectability and persons who indulge in such practices are acclaimed as most successful in their respective profession.
This is a dangerous trend, if unchecked would undermine the judicial process.
As the existing law is inadequate to check this malady, the Court not only have to be careful in adjudicating such claims but also find ways to prevent such abuse.

They have to balance the interest of these accident victims and their legal heirs on one side, by giving them just compensation at the earliest, thus giving effect to the mandate of the parliament, and on the other hand, to see that the very process is not abused and exploited by a handful of persons, who have attained specialization in this field, to make personal gains at the cost of the exchequer.
An onerous responsibility lies on the Courts.

Therefore, it is imperative that a strong message is to be sent to the abusers of the judicial process to discourage them from indulging in such practices as well as the consequences of such abuse may result in foisting the liability exclusively on the insured-owner of the vehicle".
(Emphasis supplied)

4 13.

Similarly another coordinate bench of this Court in para No.15 of the judgment in Mahadevi W/o. Shrishail Kore and Others vs. Shivaputra and Another3 held that, when the claimant came before the Tribunal alleging that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of insured vehicle, the burden of proving the said fact is on him.

entities.text: Mahadevi W/o. Shrishail Kore and Others vs. Shivaputra and Another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further held that, mere charge sheet if the same is deficient in M.F.A.No.201689/2016 DD 20.11.2020 truth does not bar the Tribunal in evaluating the other evidence.
It further held that, the insurance company cannot be saddled with the burden of challenging the charge sheet and the insurance company not challenging the charge sheet cannot be
a circumstance which is raised against it in MACT proceedings
The reading of the above judgments makes it clear that the charge sheet is not the ultimatum for the Courts nor the same is the conclusive proof.
At the most, that maybe a circumstance which has to be considered along with other materials on records.
15. Admittedly, the appellant was taken to Bannur medical center soon after the accident.
RW.1 is the Doctor who attended to him in the said hospital and made entries with regard to the accident in MLC register.
Ex. R.1
MLC register extract and the evidence of RW.1 shows that at the earliest point of time, the appellant was taken to the said hospital with a history of self-fall near Chamanahalli village at 8.30 p.m.
The said entries in Ex.R1 were not disputed.

It was only suggested to RW.1 that in case of accident there is a chance of the people who gathered in the hospital giving an incorrect history.
- 10
- Admittedly, the appellant was taken to the hospital by his relative Shivaraju who then filed complaint.

Ex. R1 shows that it was Shivaraju who had taken the victim to the hospital and then the appellant should have examined the said Shivaraju to explain the said circumstance of somebody allegedly giving the history before RW.1.
In the cross examination of RW.1, his evidence that the victim was brought by Shivaraju and he gave the history of accident was not impeached.
16. So far as the evidence of CW.1 and Ex.C1 after the preliminary treatment in Bannur hospital, the appellant was taken to Nagarajegowda Memorial Hospital, Mysuru.
As per Ex.C1 he was purportedly admitted in the said hospital at 11.05 p.m.
Ex.C1 is the case sheet of the appellant maintained in Nagarajegowda Memorial Hospital, Mysuru.
In the said document there is no mention of Shivaraju taking the appellant to the hospital.
The attendant's name is mentioned as one Basavaraju, there also only history of RTA near Chamanahalli village is mentioned.
There is no mention of the involvement of Canter vehicle.
17. Ex.C.11 was purported to be relied again as the MLC register extract.
The original MLC register was not brought - 11 - before the Court.
No seal or signature of anybody is affixed to alleged entries relating to the appellant.

In that document there is mention of Canter bearing registration No.KA.10-1194 Sri. Mahadeva vs Sri. Huchegowda on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137471706/
5 (Tempo).
CW.1 in his cross-examination though admits that he has made those entries, but states that he does not know who has given such history and under which circumstance.

CW.1 claims that the appellant was presented before him with history of road traffic accident on that day at 9.30 p.m.
Time also does not tally with the time of the accident in other records.

If CW.1 had treated the appellant in Nagarajegowda Memorial Hospital, then Ex.C1 the case sheet which also contains the consent letter and particulars of patient at the time of admission should have reflected that the appellant was hit by canter vehicle.
In Ex.C1 it is not even mentioned that he was brought with history of road traffic accident.
But he was said to have been brought with history of alleged road traffic accident.
18. The above facts and circumstances go to show that after shifting the appellant from Bannur Hospital, some improvements were made in the version of the accident.

Under such circumstances,
the entries made in the medical records at the first instance were rightly accepted by the Tribunal.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in para 3 of the judgment in Gourabai's case referred to supra held that the doctor will not take signature on piece of papers mentioning something which is incorrect.
Under the circumstances to dispel the entry in Ex.R1, the appellant was bound to examine Shivaraju.

He has no explanation for withholding such material witnesses.
20.

After such improvement in the second hospital, the complaint was purportedly filed on 01.11.2018 at 7.15 p.m., Ex.P1 itself shows that first information report was delivered to the Court on 02.11.2018 at 11.00 a.m.
Such delay in delivering the first information report also leads to inference that there is deliberation to plant the vehicle insured.

Under the circumstances, the Tribunal rightly declined to accept Ex.P7 the charge sheet as conclusive proof of rashness and negligence on the part of the driver of the canter vehicle or involvement of the said vehicle.
21. At the fag end of the arguments, learned Counsel for the appellant submits that the matter may be remanded for examination of Shivaraju, the author of Ex.C11.
It is settled law - 13 - that matters cannot be remanded at the fall of hats, unless the conditions mentioned in Order XLI Rule 23 of the Civil Procedure Code are satisfied.
This matter is pending since 2018.
Even before this Court no application was filed to adduce additional evidence.
To plug loopholes the matters cannot be remanded.
Therefore, the said prayer is liable to be rejected.
There is no merit in the appeal.

Hence, the following:
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
